To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,6t{e}^{({t}^{2}-1)}⟩\,\text{d}t=⟨\int \operatorname{sec}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t\,\text{d}t,\,\int 6t{e}^{({t}^{2}-1)}\,\text{d}t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

- For $x(t)=\operatorname{sec}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x(t)\,\text{d}t=\int \operatorname{sec}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t\,\text{d}t=\operatorname{sec}⁡t+{c}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

- For $y(t)=6t{e}^{({t}^{2}-1)},$ we calculate its integral using substitution. So, we let $u={t}^{2}-1.$ Then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=2t\,⟹\,\text{d}t=\frac{1}{2t}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,  we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int y(t)\,\text{d}t & =\int 6t{e}^{({t}^{2}-1)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 6t{e}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2t}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\int {e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3{e}^{u}+{c}_{2} \\  & =3{e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+{c}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,6t{e}^{({t}^{2}-1)}⟩\,\text{d}t & =⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t+{c}_{1},\,3{e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,3{e}^{{t}^{2}-1}⟩+⟨{c}_{1},\,{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,3{e}^{{t}^{2}-1}⟩+C.\end{aligned}
$$
